<a id="PreviewOnGitHub"></a>

### When the preview runs on GitHub, and what it keeps there

`PreviewOnGitHub` · `src/sdlc.ts:372`

By hand from GitHub, and at each push on main; on GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 machine, with Node.js 22, the version Trame runs on here (its types are those of Node 22). What it publishes (the page, as its workflow says) GitHub keeps thirty days: a preview is looked at, then replaced. The evidence is kept too, ninety days, whatever the preview answered: a refused preview says why, and someone reads it later.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| on | { manual: true, branches: main } |
| runsOn | ubuntu-24.04 |
| node | 22 |
| artefacts | { days: 30, evidence: { days: 90 } } |

- Decided by: ghalaax
- Rejected: At each pull request, a preview is placed where it is served: a pull request would place a page nobody merged; On a schedule, nothing changes the page between two pushes; The evidence not kept, what was checked, by whom and on which page would stay on a machine GitHub throws away; GitHub's ninety days for the page too, a preview replaced every push need not stay three months
- Sets the writer of: [The preview's workflow](#PreviewWorkflow)

## Architecture decision

<a id="SdlcInTheGraph"></a>

### The SDLC is in the graph

`SdlcInTheGraph` · `src/sdlc.ts:454` · status: **unknown**

What makes a version of Poselia available is declared with the rest: its artefact, the checks and the review it requires and who signs them, the programs that check and deploy it, tested in memory; trame ship runs it and keeps the evidence. The rules of the graph are rules of the std library, applied with their parameters.

Context: A version reached people when its author had looked at it: what was checked, by whom, on which page, was nowhere.

Consequences: trame ship refuses a version while a check, a review or a scenario does not hold, says whose it is, and keeps the dossier of each version shipped.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| A script of continuous integration beside the graph | the steps and their reasons would live in two places, and the graph would not know what was checked |
| A review in a pull request | it says neither which rows were seen nor in which language; a change to a row would not undo it |

- Decided by: ghalaax
- Serves: [Content checked by people who practise](product.md#CheckedContent), [Practise yoga on one's own, guided](product.md#PractiseGuided)
- Applied by: [A preview](#Preview), [A public version](#PublicVersion), [The page opens](#PageOpens), [On a phone](#OnAPhone), [The content, reviewed](#ContentReviewed), [Open the page](#OpenThePage), [Place the page](#PlaceThePage), [Code serves the product](#CodeServesTheProduct), [Each decision of architecture serves the product](#AdrsServeTheProduct), [The preview's workflow](#PreviewWorkflow), [The preview's script](#PreviewScript), [The files that run it elsewhere](#RunnersWritten)

    placed: (from: string, to: string) => `${from} placed at ${to}`,

## Policies

<a id="PreviewMode"></a>

### The way of a preview

`PreviewMode` · `src/sdlc.ts:310`

For its author and the few people they show it to: the code verified (a gap said), the page checked by programs, the rules held, the packages safe, what the device keeps migrated; and the foundations, as always.

And, as every policy, the foundations: no literal in a body, and a sound graph (nothing undecided, no error of the graph).

- Owner: ghalaax
- Its obligations: [The code shown is verified, a gap said](#CodeVerifiedSaid), [The page is checked by programs](#ProgramChecks), [The rules of the app hold](#RulesHeld), [The packages are safe](#PackagesSafe), [What the device keeps, migrated](#KeptMigrates)
